Internal helper: the file a saved result or a built table is saved in

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_result_save_file.Rd

Session 429 (reversing Session 406's stop, which gave base R's saveRDS() and readRDS() lines; Jeff: "Let's reverse the decision and incorporate the rest of your ideas"). jsave() keeps a saved result – what an analysis function returns – or a table jtable() built in R format (.rds), the one format that holds any R object. The file name is optional: jsave(m1) names the file for the object, m1.rds (a place, lst$m1, for its last part); a name with no extension gets .rds, as a data frame's does, and so does one whose ending is no file format's (model.1, so that jload("model.1") finds model.1.rds). The checks run before anything is written, in this order, each a stop whose line runs:

  • a file name typed without its quotes: ruling R18's pointer (.jst_free_text_arg(), .jst_bare_path_stop());

  • a file name that is not text;

  • an object with no name of its own – a result made in the call, a place reached by position – and no file name: the call with one;

  • another file format: only R format holds one, with the save in R format – a table, or a .docx file named, first offered the jtable() line that writes Word;

  • an input only a data frame takes (preserve.declarations =, clean.names =): the call without it.

Usage

.jst_result_save_file(
  data_sub,
  val,
  file_sub,
  file_fn,
  env,
  cl,
  mc,
  overwrite,
  data_only
)

Arguments

data_sub

The data argument as typed.

val

Its value, a saved result or a built table.

file_sub

The file argument as typed, or NULL.

file_fn

A function forcing the file argument, or NULL; called only after the unquoted-name checks, so a bare word never reaches R.

env

The caller's environment.

cl, mc

The call as typed and the matched call.

overwrite

The call's overwrite =.

data_only

The data-frame inputs the call gave, as "name =".

Value

A list: file (the name to save under, ending .rds), name (what the Saved line calls it), noun (what it is, in words) and load (the line that loads it back).
